title: 'Tools don't have independent values — their values are human values': Quote of the day by Stanford professor Fei-Fei Li on building ethical AI
excerpt: Developing AI as a tool means recognizing that its values are reflected in the values of those who build and deploy it
content_html:
With AI advancing in capability and availability, many scientists and experts have begun highlighting the risks of deploying this emerging technology. There's an overriding desire to deploy AI ethically, or to instill models with human-based values, but it remains to be seen how to standardize such an approach or even whether to regulate the industry. That's where organizations like the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI (HAI) come in.

Computer says no

When interviewed for the journal Issues in Science and Technology, the so-called 'Godmother of AI' Fei-Fei Li tried to explain how scientists and engineers can build AI that truly adheres to our values.

Quote of the day

This article is part of TechRadar Pro's QOTD project to provide an insight into the minds of the brightest and most recognized figures in the technology industry today and in years gone by. Read the full series here.

Her thesis around the responsible use of AI centers not on anthropomorphizing AI or considering it an intelligence capable of navigating the world and arriving at its own independent conclusions. Rather, it will reflect the values that we instill into it, whether that's through training or continued use of these tools.

She added in this interview that it's also about recognizing that AI, as any tool, can both empower and harm humans.

Values-driven AI

The organization that the American computer scientist leads, HAI, is an interdisciplinary research center that focuses on how best to guide AI development so that it benefits humanity and doesn't incur or lead to harm.

In recent years, there's also been an increased emphasis on whether to regulate AI nationally (or even globally) and what shape that might take. Doing so, however, is far easier said than done, with progress occurring at different paces, in different guises, and inconsistently across oceans.

There are, for example, different values that different nations or groups of people may wish to instill into the AI models they build that clash with the values of others.

content_html_zh:
随着人工智能在能力和可用性方面的进步，许多科学家和专家已经开始强调部署这种新兴技术的风险。 人们迫切希望以合乎道德的方式部署人工智能，或者向模型灌输以人为本的价值观，但如何标准化这种方法，甚至是否对行业进行监管，还有待观察。 这就是斯坦福以人为中心的人工智能研究所 (HAI) 等组织发挥作用的地方。

在接受《科学与技术》杂志采访时，被称为“人工智能教母”的李飞飞试图解释科学家和工程师如何构建真正符合我们价值观的人工智能。

她的论文围绕负责任地使用人工智能，而不是将人工智能拟人化或认为它是一种能够驾驭世界并得出自己独立结论的智能。 相反，它将反映我们灌输给它的价值观，无论是通过培训还是持续使用这些工具。

她在这次采访中补充说，这还在于认识到人工智能作为任何工具，既可以赋予人类权力，也可以伤害人类。

价值观驱动的人工智能

美国计算机科学家领导的组织 HAI 是一个跨学科研究中心，专注于如何最好地指导人工智能的发展，使其造福人类，而不招致或导致伤害。

近年来，人们也越来越重视是否在国家（甚至全球）范围内监管人工智能以及可能采取何种形式。 然而，这样做说起来容易做起来难，因为进展速度不同、形式不同，而且跨越海洋的情况也不一致。

例如，不同国家或人群可能希望将不同的价值观灌输到他们构建的人工智能模型中，这些价值观与其他人的价值观发生冲突。
